questions.question: How did the French Revolution influence Romantic poets in England?
questions.solution_html:
• French Revolution deeply impacted Romanticism - inspiring and complicating its themes
  • - writers were drawn to the revolution’s ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity, which
  • aligned with their emphasis on individual freedom - rebellion against authority - William
  • Wordsworth’s belief in the transformative power of political upheaval – Coleridge
  • voicing concerns about the potential for tyranny and chaos – Shelley - emphasized the
  • need for moral and spiritual transformation alongside political change - these poets
  • highlight the complex relationship between Romanticism and the French Revolution
  • showing how it influenced their exploration of freedom, human nature, and the emotional
  • cost of political change.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Attempt a note on Victorian Dilemma and Compromise.
questions.solution_html:
• Victorian Dilemma - conflict between faith and doubt, duty and desire, tradition and
  • reform - generated a creative ferment - a search for new syntheses and ways of being
  • managed this dilemma through the Victorian Compromise - a flexible yet uneasy
  • synthesis. Public life continued to reflect Christian moral codes and imperial pride
  • private, individuals increasingly questioned authority and explored new worldviews
  • Charitable endeavours and reformist zeal softened capitalism - Science was often
  • embraced - religion retained its social authority - the language of humanitarianism
  • softened imperial rhetoric - this balancing act preserved social cohesion in an era of
  • profound upheaval.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How did the Home Rule Movement lead to the political division of Ireland and what were its consequences?
questions.solution_html:
• A long political campaign - aimed to give Ireland its own parliament - more control over
  • its internal affairs - began in 1870, led by Isaac Butt - the British Parliament passed the
  • Government of Ireland Act in 1920 - proposed the creation of two separate parliaments
  • one for Northern Ireland and one for Southern Ireland - the struggle between Irish
  • nationalists and British forces continued - Anglo-Irish Treaty of 1921- created the Irish
  • Free State - a self-governing nation separate from the United Kingdom - showed the
  • inability of Britain to manage the demands of different national groups within its empire
  • demonstrated that legal reforms through Parliament were not enough to resolve deep
  • divisions, based on religion and national identity - the movement helped pave the way for
  • the later creation of devolved governments in Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
questions.final_answer: the later creation of devolved governments in Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss how Percy Bysshe Shelley uses mythological and natural imagery to articulate his radical political and philosophical ideals in works like "Prometheus Unbound" and "Ode to the West Wind."
questions.solution_html:
• Prometheus Unbound reworks Greek myth - depict the overthrow of tyranny and the
  • triumph of love and imagination - the figure of Prometheus symbolises spiritual resistance
  • and human potential - reflecting utopian vision of social renewal Shelley’s use of myth is
  • more abstract and philosophical - In “Ode to the West Wind”, the titular force is
  • personified as a divine power - reminiscent of Greek elemental deities - invocation of the
  • Mediterranean as a dreaming figure and the “Maenad”- like storm fuse natural phenomena
  • with classical ecstasy - Greek mythology becomes a symbolic system - to explore themes
  • of renewal, revolution, and the sublime - use of Greek forms is imaginative - revives their
  • spirit to support a radical poetic vision.
questions.final_answer: spirit to support a radical poetic vision
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: In what ways did new inventions change daily life in the Victorian era?
questions.solution_html:
• Victorian era - defined by unprecedented technological innovation, industrial expansion
  • and sweeping social transformation - the expansion of railways, steamships, and
  • mechanised production reshaped both the economy and society - with technological
  • innovations such as the telephone, electric lighting and the early automobile, the period
  • was defined by modern advancement - Innovation extended into communications
  • medicine, domestic life, and education - the telegraph, enabled near-instantaneous long
  • distance communication - electricity began to replace gas lighting in both factories and
  • homes. Key inventions of the era included the sewing machine, the typewriter, the camera
  • and steam-powered vehicles laid the groundwork for the modern automobile - the steam
  • engine - sewing machines and sanitation advances - changed domestic routines - Steam
  • power revolutionised manufacturing and transportation, powering locomotives
  • steamships, and mechanised factories - railway lines crisscrossed Britain, connecting rural
  • and urban areas, enhancing trade, and granting people unprecedented mobility.
questions.final_answer: and urban areas, enhancing trade, and granting people unprecedented mobility
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How did the Home Rule Movement lead to the political division of Ireland and what were its consequences?
questions.solution_html:
• A long political campaign - aimed to give Ireland its own parliament - more control over
  • its internal affairs - began in 1870, led by Isaac Butt - the British Parliament passed the
  • Government of Ireland Act in 1920 - proposed the creation of two separate parliaments
  • one for Northern Ireland and one for Southern Ireland - the struggle between Irish
  • nationalists and British forces continued - Anglo-Irish Treaty of 1921- created the Irish
  • Free State - a self-governing nation separate from the United Kingdom - showed the
  • inability of Britain to manage the demands of different national groups within its empire
  • demonstrated that legal reforms through Parliament were not enough to resolve deep
  • divisions, based on religion and national identity - the movement helped pave the way for
  • the later creation of devolved governments in Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
questions.final_answer: the later creation of devolved governments in Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland

questions.question: In what ways did new inventions change daily life in the Victorian era?

  • and sweeping social transformation - the expansion of railways, steamships, and
  • mechanised production reshaped both the economy and society - with technological
  • innovations such as the telephone, electric lighting and the early automobile, the period
  • was defined by modern advancement - Innovation extended into communications
  • medicine, domestic life, and education - the telegraph, enabled near-instantaneous long
  • distance communication - electricity began to replace gas lighting in both factories and
  • homes. Key inventions of the era included the sewing machine, the typewriter, the camera
  • and steam-powered vehicles laid the groundwork for the modern automobile - the steam
  • engine - sewing machines and sanitation advances - changed domestic routines - Steam
  • power revolutionised manufacturing and transportation, powering locomotives
  • steamships, and mechanised factories - railway lines crisscrossed Britain, connecting rural
  • and urban areas, enhancing trade, and granting people unprecedented mobility.
questions.final_answer: and urban areas, enhancing trade, and granting people unprecedented mobility
